themes.summary: SpaceX priced its IPO on June 11 and began trading June 12 on Nasdaq (SPCX), raising $75B — the largest IPO of all time — at an implied ~$1.75T valuation. The deal crystalizes SpaceX's AI compute revenue (~$2B/month from Anthropic and Google) as core to its bull case alongside Starlink profitability.

themes.theme: AI foundation labs racing to public markets
themes.summary: OpenAI filed a confidential IPO registration with the SEC and plans a pre-IPO tender offer at its $852B valuation. Anthropic, coming off a $65B primary round, is positioning for a late-summer public offering. The looming AI pricing war — OpenAI considering drastic token price cuts to compete with Anthropic — may be subsidized entirely by pre-IPO capital.

themes.theme: Prometheus: Bezos bets $12B on industrial AI
themes.summary: Prometheus, Jeff Bezos's industrial AI startup targeting an 'artificial general engineer' to compress manufacturing cycle times, closed a $12B Series B at a $41B valuation led by JPMorgan, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, and DST Global. An unconfirmed $100B affiliated holding company aimed at acquiring legacy industrial companies as training-data sources was also reported.

Apollo and Blackstone partnered with Broadcom to back a $35B private credit facility enabling Anthropic to lease Google-designed chips via Fluidstack data centers, targeting 20+ GW compute capacity through 2028. KKR simultaneously launched Helix Digital Infrastructure with $10B initial commitments from Kuwait Investment Authority, Nvidia, and Vistra, led by ex-AWS CEO Adam Selipsky.

Neura Robotics (Germany) raised €1.4B Series C backed by Tether, Qualcomm, Amazon, Nvidia, Bosch, Schaeffler, and EIB. Theker (Spain) raised $85M Series A led by CRV with Samsung and LVMH. Standard Bots raised $200M at a $1B valuation. Robotics has become a consensus category for crossover and strategic investors.

Flutter Entertainment (FanDuel/Betfair parent) announced plans to delist from the LSE, joining CRH (delisted April) and Wise (primary moved to New York in May). The SpaceX IPO priced on Nasdaq rather than anywhere in Europe, further consolidating the narrative of US capital markets dominance.

SFR ($23.5B acquisition by three French telecoms), Banca Monte dei Paschi ($35B Intesa offer), DCC (£5.7B KKR/ECP), Tate & Lyle (£3.7B Ingredion), Kontron (€1.47B Ennoconn), and Hugo Boss (€2.7B Frasers bid) all moved in one week, suggesting European corporate assets are clearing after years of strategic paralysis.
